money_at_stake.rationale: Deliberately built from concrete pools this occurrence is actually moving money through, not the headline value of oil transiting Hormuz. The US government's DFC stood up a $20bn Gulf marine war-risk reinsurance facility with Chubb as lead underwriter within weeks of the war starting, a real committed capacity figure. Iran's own ad hoc transit toll is separately estimated at up to $3bn a year now and toward $8bn a year at pre-conflict traffic. War-risk premiums for the route rose from about 0.25% to as high as 10% of hull value, a roughly 4,000% peak spike, sustained for five-plus months rather than a one-day print. None of these three pools alone clears $100bn, so GT_100B is not supported; together with the freight-rate windfall documented under capture_odds they are comfortably above the $10bn floor, so B10_100 fits better than B1_10. The $1.2 trillion figure for annual Gulf trade flows at risk is cited for scale but deliberately not used to justify GT_100B: it is the value of trade exposed to disruption, not a spend or revenue pool any chain participant collects, and folding it in would be exactly the imprecision the reference appraisal for SIG-20260829-01 warned against.

public_reach.rationale: Genuinely split down the middle rather than rounded toward either extreme, so scored at the center of the 40-60 mixed range. For reach: the DFC facility's lead underwriter is Chubb, listed on the NYSE under ticker CB, and the freight-rate windfall documented under capture_odds accrues largely to crude-tanker owners, a shipping segment that (unlike the private Arctic yards in SIG-20260829-01) skews heavily toward publicly listed operators. Against reach: Iran's own toll revenue, plausibly the single largest identified pool by rate of collection, was administered through the Persian Gulf Strait Authority, an Iranian state-established body the US later sanctioned, so it cannot be reached by any brokerage account; and the maritime-security layer this signal's own thesis names as one of its four pillars sits inside a roughly $28.6bn (2026) market whose named participants in the cited industry report are specialist firms (Constellis, Ambrey, Trident Ltd. and others) that this appraisal did not individually confirm are absent from public listings, so that point is treated as a plausible but unverified reach constraint rather than a sourced fact. No source quantifies the split by percentage, so the 50 reflects that a real reachable slice and a real, more firmly evidenced unreachable slice (the toll) both exist, not that the money is more likely to reach issuers than not.

capture_odds.rationale: Real, already-realized pricing power on two fronts, which is why this sits above the 40 price-taker anchor, but not at 85+ because the government backstop and the war's own on-off volatility cap how much of that pricing power is durable. Tanker owners captured an already-realized windfall: the VLCC benchmark hit an all-time high of $423,736/day within days of the war's start, up more than 94% in a single session, as major war-risk insurers pulled coverage from vessels in the Persian Gulf. Insurers show a favorable premium-to-claims profile so far: premiums near 10% of hull value have been sustained for five-plus months while the signal's own evidence records only three tanker hijackings (of four vessels total seized by Somali pirates in the same window) in that period, i.e. claims paid look small next to premium collected. Held below 85 because (a) the DFC facility is a government-created reinsurance backstop, meaning part of the risk-bearing (and by implication some of the pricing signal) is not pure private-market capture, and (b) the war has already shown a ceasefire-then-breakdown cycle (April ceasefire, June MOU, collapse in July), so today's elevated rate is evidenced but not proven durable for the full horizon.

timing_fit.rationale: Scored at the top anchor because the money is not projected into the window, it has been moving inside it continuously since within days of the anchor_date and is still moving as of this appraisal. The DFC facility had Chubb named lead underwriter within about two weeks of the February 28, 2026 anchor_date, with coverage later expanded to include liability; war-risk premiums have stayed elevated for five-plus months rather than spiking once and normalizing; and as of August 26, 2026, four days before this appraisal, there is still no ceasefire and no active US-Iran negotiating track (an Iran-Oman technical dialogue over a temporary corridor continues, but that falls short of a US-Iran resolution), with Iran's IRGC stating the strait stays closed until its terms are met. Not scored above 85 because the occurrence's own window states 'no resolution in sight' rather than a fixed multi-year program, so how much of the 2-4 year horizon this state persists for is itself the open question a ceasefire could compress at any point.

notes.text: LEAKY here comes from a genuinely mixed public_reach (50, not a low outlier) rather than a near-total leak like SIG-20260829-01: real listed exposure exists through crude-tanker owners and Chubb as the DFC facility's lead underwriter, but it sits beside two large unreachable-or-uncertain pools (Iran's own toll revenue and the private-contractor-heavy maritime security layer) that the signal's own thesis treats as core, not incidental. A chain build here should start from marine war-risk reinsurance and tanker-owner economics, where the listed set actually sits, rather than from the toll or the piracy/security layer, which are the parts of this thesis most likely to stay outside a brokerage account.
